observations: Photo 0 shows a used car engine assembly on a concrete floor, likely in a workshop or yard.
The engine has visible components: intake manifold, timing belt pulley, alternator, and various hoses and wires.
There is a label on the side of the engine block, but the text is too blurry to read.
The engine appears dirty and used, with some rust and grime visible.
No visible branding or model number is legible in the photo.
The seller claims it is a 'Direct tokumbo' (imported from Belgium) with a 2-month guarantee and that it is 'Tested ok'.

claims.evidence: No proof of origin or warranty in the photo. The label on the engine block is unreadable.
No video or photo of the engine running or being tested. No proof of functionality.

claims.claim: Tokunbo, direct from Belgium. Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Engine may be damaged or non-functional
risks.proof: Video or photo of the engine running, or a close-up of the internal components (e.g., cylinder head, crankshaft) to check for wear or damage.

risks.risk: Engine may not be from a compatible vehicle or may be stolen or salvaged
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine block with visible casting number or VIN tag, or a photo of the vehicle it was removed from.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown origin, which reduces value

risks.risk: Engine may have hidden mechanical issues (e.g., seized, worn bearings)
risks.proof: Photo of the engine from the front and back, showing the crankshaft and cylinder bores, or a video of the engine being turned over.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine block showing casting number or VIN tag.
Video or photo of the engine running or being tested.
Photo of the vehicle it was removed from, if available.
Photo of the engine from the front and back to check for damage or wear.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
